title: Critical Java vulnerability discovered; NIS issues urgent inspection advisory to public institutions
text:

 🌐 日本語 · 中文 · हिन्दी · Español · العربية · Français · বাংলা · Русский · Deutsch Shin Jung-hwan Reporter 입력 2026.11.17 23:35 ( 연합뉴스 ) A critical vulnerability has been discovered in Java, which is widely used in public, financial, and corporate systems, that allows for remote code execution without an authentication process. The National Intelligence Service has advised public institutions to inspect their Java runtime environments and internet-exposed systems and prepare for security updates.
 NIS Recommends Inspection of Java Runtime Environments
 The National Cyber Security Center under the National Intelligence Service delivered a "Recommendation for Preparing Preparatory Measures for the Announcement of Java Vulnerabilities" to public institutions on the 17th. The content advises institutions to identify systems that may be affected by checking the versions, detailed builds, and operating systems of the Java currently in operation.
 The scope of response must be verified by examining not only the Java installed on servers but also runtime environments embedded in applications and container images. Organizations were also instructed to re-examine the list of systems and services exposed to the internet and to block external access not required for business operations.
 Remote Code Execution Possible Without Authentication
 A vulnerability has been identified in Java applications that allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code remotely without separate authentication. The risk level is 9.2 out of 10 based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, which is at the highest "critical" level.
 If an attack is successful, information may be leaked or services may be disrupted depending on system permissions and configurations. The international common security vulnerability identifier has been reserved as CVE-2026-114938.
 Confirmation Required by OpenJDK Distribution
 Products identified as potentially vulnerable include OpenJDK version 17.0.6 or higher, an open-source environment used for the development and execution of Java programs. Since the OpenJDK family is provided by various companies as separate distributions, the release timing of modified versions and version labeling may differ.
 Rather than judging solely on the basis of using Java 17, companies and institutions must verify the JVM, vendor, and distribution actually in operation. It is necessary to examine whether related distributions, in addition to Oracle Java SE, are included in the operating environment.
 Preparation of Recovery Procedures for Security Updates
 The NIS requested that institutions verify compatibility for each product so that security updates can be applied immediately upon release and to prepare backup and recovery procedures in case of failures during the update process.
 Oracle announced its important security update schedule on the 17th, focusing on high-risk vulnerabilities including Java. A total of 652 new security patches are scheduled to be distributed for all Oracle products, and it is known that 11 security patches are included in the Java SE sector.
 Java is used for the development and execution of various programs including financial transactions, e-commerce, and public administrative services. Institutions and companies that operate major business systems must check detailed attack conditions, the range of affected services, and modified versions for each distribution according to the guidance of each vendor once security patches are released.
